proof.text: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D)$ be strict and set $H(a,d)=F(a)(d)$. For homogeneous $\alpha:a\to a'$ and $\delta:d\to d'$, define $H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=F(\alpha)_{d'}F(a)(\delta)$. The cited enriched naturality equation is $F(a')(\epsilon)F(\alpha)_{d'}=(-1)^{|\alpha||\epsilon|}F(\alpha)_{d''}F(a)(\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon:d'\to d''$. Thus, for $\beta:a'\to a''$, $H(\beta\otimes\epsilon)H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=(-1)^{|\epsilon||\alpha|}F(\beta\alpha)_{d''}F(a)(\epsilon\delta)$, which is the specified tensor composition. Writing $\partial$ for the Hom differential, the chain-map actions and Leibniz rule give $\partial H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=H(d\alpha\otimes\delta)+(-1)^{|\alpha|}H(\alpha\otimes d\delta)$. Bilinearity therefore gives a chain map on each tensor Hom complex. Units are preserved, so $H$ is a covariant dg module.

proof.text: Conversely, let $H$ be a module over $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$. Put $F(a)(d)=H(a,d)$, $B_a(\delta)=H(1_a\otimes\delta)$ and $A_d(\alpha)=H(\alpha\otimes1_d)$. These restrictions are chain maps and preserve the respective compositions and units. The tensor composition gives $B_{a'}(\delta)A_d(\alpha)=(-1)^{|\alpha||\delta|}H(\alpha\otimes\delta)$ and $A_{d'}(\alpha)B_a(\delta)=H(\alpha\otimes\delta)$. Hence $B_{a'}(\delta)A_d(\alpha)=(-1)^{|\alpha||\delta|}A_{d'}(\alpha)B_a(\delta)$: the components $A_d(\alpha)$ form a degree-$|\alpha|$ module transformation $F(a)\to F(a')$. Restriction to the first factor also gives $\partial A_d(\alpha)=A_d(d\alpha)$ and $A_d(\beta\alpha)=A_d(\beta)A_d(\alpha)$, so $F$ is a strict dg functor into $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D)$. The factorization $H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=A_{d'}(\alpha)B_a(\delta)$ recovers $H$. Conversely, restricting the forward construction recovers $F(a)(\delta)$ and $F(\alpha)_d$ by the unit axioms, so both constructions are inverse.

proof.text: A degree-$r$ transformation between two such diagrams is a family $\eta_{a,d}$ satisfying the tensor-module equation for every homogeneous $\alpha\otimes\delta$ exactly when it satisfies the two equations for $\alpha\otimes1$ and $1\otimes\delta$: the forward implication is restriction, and the reverse implication follows by inserting the two equations into $H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=A(\alpha)B(\delta)$ and commuting the homogeneous factors with the displayed Koszul sign. Therefore the component families, their differentials $d\eta=d_G\eta-(-1)^r\eta d_F$, identities and compositions are the same complexes and operations on both sides. This is the actual enriched Hom identification, not merely a bijection of degree-zero maps.

proof.text: Under this identification the underlying maps are literally the same component families. On the diagram side, the projective structure supplied by [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] has weak equivalences the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms and fibrations the objectwise degreewise surjections; the same classes define the projective structure on modules over $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$ whenever that structure exists. Hence the trivial fibrations coincide, so their left lifting classes (the cofibrations) coincide as well. The initial maps are identified too, and therefore projective cofibrancy agrees. Applying the same observation to any iterated projective construction proves the asserted model-structure and cofibrant-object comparison without imposing a cofibrancy condition on the Hom complexes of $\mathcal D$.

title: Currying dg-module diagrams over a tensor product
statement: Use the cochain-complex and dg-category conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], the module Hom-complex conventions of [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution], and the enriched diagram conventions of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model], in sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal D$ be small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$. Let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D)$ be covariant dg functors $\mathcal D\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$; a degree-$r$ transformation $\eta:F\to G$ satisfies $G(\delta)\eta_d=(-1)^{r|\delta|}\eta_{d'}F(\delta)$ and has differential $d\eta=d_G\eta-(-1)^r\eta d_F$. Define $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$ to have object pairs, morphism complexes $\mathcal A(a,a')\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal D(d,d')$, the tensor differential, and composition $(\beta\otimes\epsilon)\circ(\alpha\otimes\delta)=(-1)^{|\epsilon||\alpha|}(\beta\alpha\otimes\epsilon\delta)$ on homogeneous morphisms. There is an isomorphism of dg categories between strict dg functors $\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D)$ and covariant dg modules over $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$. It sends $F$ to $H$ with $H(a,d)=F(a)(d)$ and $H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=F(\alpha)_{d'}F(a)(\delta)$, and identifies all transformation complexes, differentials, identities and compositions. It identifies objectwise quasi-isomorphisms and objectwise degreewise surjections, and the projective model structures (hence cofibrant objects) on both sides whenever these structures exist.
